audience: Arcade players who want a two-minute territory round with no install and no account.
core_mechanic: Close a fence loop around open ground; every cell the enemy's flood fill cannot reach is claimed as territory, and the claim target rises each level.
title: Fenceline: claim territory by closing a fence the enemy cannot flood past
why_hot: A shipped, dated example of the exact Flambeee constraint set (one file, no dependencies, no network) used for a territory mechanic, where the reverse flood fill from the enemy is a cheap, testable core rule rather than an art trick.

audience: Cozy puzzle players who want six short rooms and a quiet arrival.
core_mechanic: Your recorded movement replays as remembered selves whose light opens bridges, so the route you already took becomes the tool that solves the room.
title: Lantern Duet: your recorded path replays and lights the bridges
why_hot: A November 2026 jam build whose core rule is that your own recorded path replays alongside you and its light opens the bridges, which makes route planning recursive instead of a key hunt.

audience: Instant-play arcade players arriving from a feed with no patience for a menu.
core_mechanic: Play begins the instant the page loads, and each run ends with an automatic replay of your best line so the next attempt starts with a model to beat.
title: SKYHOP: play starts at page load and every run ends with your best line replayed
why_hot: Dated play counts behind a zero-friction start (play begins at load) and an automatic best-line replay, plus a combo rule that is one sentence long and still changes every fight.
